LESSON: SWIMMING (OPTIONAL)

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Performing and Displaying
Topic 2.6: Swimming (Optional)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Swimming (Optional), part of Performing and Displaying in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How do you describe the front crawl technique?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Swimming (Optional) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: A learner develops the skill of interacting with digital technology as they use digital devices with

appropriate assistive technology to record video clips on own and others’ performance and give constructive feedback

● Communication and collaboration: A learner develops the skill of teamwork as they work together in performing leg-action

in front-crawl development.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Safety: a learner develops the skills of personal safety as they practise the skill of front crawl while observing safety

Link to other subjects:

Science and technology: Learners will be able to relate the concept of buoyancy and floatation in science and technology as

they are exposed to floatation and buoyancy in swimming.

Suggested Assessment Resources:

Swimming facility such as standard pool, inflatable pools; Clothing and gear- such as swimsuits, goggles; safety equipment- such as life jackets, rescue tubes, first aid kit, spine board; Swimming aids- such as kickboards, pull buoys, fins, swim noodles,

floatation devices. Braille papers, Braille machines, slates and stylus.
